input.question: Oracle v. Google Law Suit
input.ground_truth: Oracle bought a company called Sun. Sun had developed a programming language called Java. Google had introduced an operating system for mobile phones called Andorid. Android is built on top of a variant of Java. Android started to become very valuable and Oracle wanted to get some of that money. Oracle claimed that Android used some things from Java that Oracle didn't explicitly license them to use. Google disagreed. A court decided, largely in favor of Google.

Question: Oracle v. Google Law Suit

Answer:

response.prediction: In the Oracle v. Google lawsuit, Oracle claimed that Google copied protected parts of Java when creating Android. Google argued that they were allowed to use certain parts of Java because it was necessary to make their software work with existing Java code. The case went to the U.S. Supreme Court, which decided that Google’s use of the Java code was considered “fair use” under copyright law. This means that, in this situation, Google did not break the law by using some of Java’s code to help build Android. The decision was important because it set a precedent about how much of someone else’s code can be used when making new software that works with existing programs.
